bull.b: Sustained top-line momentum (TTM revenue +35.1%) combined with very high gross margins (~76%–82%) provide a durable revenue and margin base. This supports scalable gross profit as launches ramp, enabling future operating leverage if SG&A/R&D growth is curtailed.

Strong launch metrics—44% sequential growth, fast payer approvals (~90%), >5,000 prescribers, >80% patient support enrollment and ~30‑day refill cadence—indicate durable adoption, reimbursement acceptance and patient retention that underpin predictable recurring product revenue.

bull.t: Stronger balance sheet and cash runway
bull.b: A meaningful reduction in debt to ~$38M, positive equity and ~ $1.2B in cash offer a multi-quarter runway to fund commercialization and late‑stage TPIP trials. Low leverage (debt/equity ~0.05) reduces refinancing risk and gives management flexibility to execute strategic plans.

bear.b: Very large operating and free cash outflows signal material burn relative to current revenue. Until the company achieves sustained cash-flow positivity, it remains dependent on execution, expense control or external financing, creating structural funding risk if revenue ramps slower than assumed.

Despite high gross margins, operating expenses far exceed gross profit, producing deep operating and net losses. Structural profitability requires sustained revenue scale or marked cost reduction; absent that, returns on capital remain negative and value creation is delayed.

Uncertainty from U.S. MFN policy and potential future payer tightening can materially delay or restrict international expansion and compress reimbursement. Combined with competing treprostinil programs, these structural access and competitive pressures could limit market share and pricing power over time.
